---
name: rewrite-text
description: Rewrite a text the user gives - make it shorter, longer, simpler, more formal, friendlier, clearer or more persuasive, or change it for a new audience - keeping its meaning and facts, and showing the result ready to use.
---
# Rewriting a text

Use this when the user gives a text and wants it changed in style, length or tone: "make this shorter", "simplify", "make it sound professional", "for a 10-year-old", "less angry", "turn these notes into a paragraph".

Steps:
1. Read the whole text and note its facts: names, numbers, dates, claims, the order of points. These stay the same unless the user asks to change them.
2. Name the one change the user wants. If the user gave no target, guess from the text: a messy text gets "clearer", a long one "shorter", a rude one "polite".
3. Rewrite the whole text. Keep the user's language. Keep the format (a list stays a list, an email stays an email).
4. Apply the target with numbers: "shorter" means half the length; "much shorter" one third; "a summary" 3 to 5 sentences; "simpler" means short sentences (up to 15 words), everyday words, one idea per sentence; "more formal" means no contractions, no slang, full sentences, a greeting and a close; "friendlier" means a warm opening line, "you" and "we", no commands.
5. Give the rewritten text first, in full. Then one line that says what you changed ("shortened from 180 to 85 words, removed the repeated apology"). Nothing else unless asked.

Defaults:
- Never add new facts, claims or promises. Never drop a number, a date, a name or a condition.
- When shortening, cut repetition, filler and explanations first; cut facts last, and say which ones you cut.
- When simplifying, replace a hard word with an easy one, not with a longer explanation.
- When the text is in bad grammar, fix the grammar while you rewrite; do not comment on it.

Output template:
<the rewritten text>

Changed: <one line>

Example:
User: "Make this shorter: 'I am writing to you today because I wanted to let you know that unfortunately I will not be able to attend the meeting on Thursday due to the fact that I have a doctor's appointment that I cannot move.'"
Good answer: "I can't attend Thursday's meeting; I have a doctor's appointment I cannot move." / Changed: 41 words to 14, same facts.

Do:
- Keep the author's voice when the request is only "shorter" or "clearer".
- Keep the order of the points unless the order is the problem.
Don't:
- Don't give three versions when one was asked for.
- Don't explain writing rules; just apply them.
- Don't change the meaning to make the text nicer.

Before you answer, check: every fact of the original is still there or named as cut; the length matches the target; the language is the user's; the format is kept; the one "Changed" line is there.
